newsitem.title: USA: Appalachian Power files $75 mln debt shelf.
newsitem.headline: Appalachian Power files $75 mln debt shelf.

text.p: Appalachian Power said Friday it filed a shelf registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission to sell up to $75 million in debt securities.
When combined with a previous registration, Appalachian, a unit of American Electric Power Co Inc, will have a total offering of $100 million in securities available for sale, the filing said.

Proceeds will be used to refund long-term debt, to fund the construction program, or to repay short-term unsecured indebtedness incurred in connection with its construction program, the company said in the filing.
The debt securities will consist of first mortgage bonds, designated secured medium term notes and/or unsecured debt securities (notes), the filing said.
The company's first mortgage bonds, 9.35 percent series due 2021 ($43,250,000) may be redeemed at their regular redemption price of 107.02 percent.

Appalachian Power is engaged in the generation, purchase, transmission and distribution of electric power to about 865,000 customers in Virginia and West Virginia and in supplying electric power at wholesale to other electric utility companies and muncipalities in those states and Tennessee.
